title: Who weeps for God?
hookLine: a schoolteacher with a notebook, and a priest who asks who weeps for God
carry: long for god the way lungs want air
tomorrow: The snake that was told not to bite
last: HUMBLER THAN A BLADE OF GRASS.

cards: A schoolteacher keeps a diary. That sounds like nothing.

But this one comes home from visits to a temple garden north of Calcutta and writes down, as exactly as he can, what a priest there said that day: the jokes, the songs, the questions, who was sitting in the room.
He signs his work with a single letter: M. Those pages became a book in Bengali, the Kathamrita, and in English, the Gospel of Sri Ramakrishna. The modern teachers begin with the man in that room.

teach.b: Ramakrishna served as a priest at the Kali temple at Dakshineswar, on the bank of the Ganges.
The stories about him keep returning to one thing: he longed for God, for the Divine Mother, with an intensity that alarmed the people around him.
Tradition says that as a young priest he would weep at the end of a day: another day gone, Mother, and still you haven't shown yourself.

Years later, with visitors from the city in his room, he kept coming back to that longing. In the Gospel he says, in effect: people shed jugs of tears over their wives and children, over money and property.
Who weeps for God? And he tells a story. A disciple asked his teacher how to see God.
Come with me, the teacher said, walked him to a pond, and pushed his head under the water. Held it there. Then let him up, gasping.
What did you feel? I felt I'd die for one breath of air. When you long for God like that, the teacher said, you will see God.
It isn't a method; nobody is being told to hold anyone's head under water. It's a measurement: how much do you want this? Not cleverness first, not learning first.
Wanting God the way lungs want air.
This is the heart of bhakti as Ramakrishna taught it: longing for God, which teachers in his tradition call vyakulata, a restless yearning, matters more than learning.

teach.h: WANT GOD THE WAY LUNGS WANT AIR.
teach.b: Cry to God with a longing heart, he told his visitors, and you will see God.

how: The Gospel of Sri Ramakrishna is read aloud in study circles and at Ramakrishna centers, and devotees visit the temple garden at Dakshineswar, where his room is kept.

games.q: you've asked your teacher how to see God. he walks you down to a pond. what happens next?
o: he tells you to sit and meditate on the water.
he pushes your head under and holds it there.
he asks you to bathe and repeat a mantra.
games.why: he holds you under, then lets you up gasping. what did you feel? when you long for God the way you longed for that breath, you will see God.

practice: Ramakrishna's advice was simple: find a quiet corner and call to God the way a child calls for its mother. Try it now, silently or in a whisper, in your own words: tell God what you long for most, honestly, not politely.
If you pray to the Mother, or Krishna, or Shiva, use that name. If you don't pray, name the thing you want most underneath everything, and rest with that wanting for a few slow breaths.
